name: Walled Hilltop Village (Vila Intramuros)
tagline: Inside the castle walls, at the top of everything
description: The historic core of Marvao, whitewashed houses and cobbled lanes packed inside medieval fortifications atop the granite peak, crowned by the castle. This is the postcard version of Marvao, with the panoramic views Saramago wrote about. Quiet, car-free within the gates, and home to most guesthouses, the tourist office, and the village's few cafes and tascas.
bestFor: short scenic stays, photographers, writers seeking isolation
cons: No coworking or real work infrastructure
Very limited shops and dining choice

name: Below the Walls (Sao Salvador do Mundo / lower slopes)
tagline: The quieter foot of the hill, closer to daily life
description: The area spreading down the slopes just outside the main gates, where some newer housing, the parking areas, and a handful of residents' homes sit below the fortified core. Slightly more practical than the walled village itself, with easier car access and a short walk up into the historic center. Still small-scale and rural in character.
bestFor: longer stays needing easier parking and car access
pros: Easier parking than inside the walls
Still a short walk to the village core

name: Ammaia Ruins / Sao Salvador da Aramenha
tagline: Roman ruins and a small valley village below Marvao
description: A small village and archaeological site in the valley beneath Marvao, home to the excavated Roman city of Ammaia and its interpretation center. A quieter, flatter alternative base with a more agricultural feel, popular for a half-day history detour rather than daily errands. Roughly a 10 to 15 minute drive from the hilltop village.
bestFor: history lovers, day-trippers, those wanting flatter terrain
pros: Access to genuine Roman archaeological site
Flatter, easier terrain than the hilltop
cons: Very limited amenities of its own
Still requires a car for everything

name: Castelo de Vide / Portalegre area
tagline: The nearest real towns, for services and a bigger base
description: Castelo de Vide, another striking hilltop village around 20 minutes away, and Portalegre, the district capital about 25 minutes from Marvao, are the practical service hubs for the area, offering supermarkets, hospitals, more restaurants, and better connectivity. Many people who love Marvao's setting choose to base themselves here instead and visit Marvao regularly.
vibe: small-town, more amenities, still rural Alentejo
bestFor: those wanting Marvao's scenery with more day-to-day convenience
pros: Better wifi and more dining options
Still close enough for regular Marvao visits
cons: Loses the immediate hilltop atmosphere of Marvao itself
